A 25-year-old male presents with a 2-month history of recurring palpitations. He reports a childhood
diagnosis of a minor cardiac defect but lacks detailed information and regular medical follow-up.
Physical examination reveals a heart murmur. The following hemodynamic measurements were
obtained during cardiac catheterization: | | Oxygen saturation (%) | Pressure (mm Hg) | | --- | --- | --- | |
Right atrium | 75 | 5 | | Right ventricle | 75 | 25/4 | | Pulmonary trunk | 75 | 22/15 | | Left atrium | 99 | 12 |
| Left ventricle | 99 | 155/10 | | Ascending aorta | 99 | 155/57 | Based on these findings, what is the most
likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Tricuspid valve regurgitation (B) Patent ductus arteriosus (C)
Coarctation of the aorta (D) Atrial septal defect (E) Aortic valve regurgitation (F) Hypertrophic
cardiomyopathy (G) Mitral valve stenosis (H) Aortic stenosis (I) Ventricular septal defect (J) Pulmonary
valve stenosis
 A. Atrial septal defect
B. Ventricular septal defect
C. Mitral valve stenosis
D. Aortic valve regurgitation
E. Coarctation of the aorta
F. Tricuspid valve regurgitation
G. Pulmonary valve stenosis
H. Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

I. Aortic stenosis
J. Patent ductus arteriosus
